items.headline_md: Steam's Personal Calendar is now a permanent store feature
items.summary_md: It recommends new and upcoming games over an 8-week window based on your playtime and wishlist.
items.details_md:
**Where to find it:** Valve says it's [right on your Steam store homepage, or at store.steampowered.com/personalcalendar](https://store.steampowered.com/news/posts/4149575031735702629). Direct link: **https://store.steampowered.com/personalcalendar**

**Click steps**
1. Sign in to Steam. It's personalized, so you need an account with playtime behind it.
2. Open the **Store** front page (in a browser or the desktop client's Store tab) and scroll to the **Personal Calendar** section, which shows this week, two weeks back, and two weeks ahead ([Steamworks docs](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/marketing/visibility/personalcalendar)).
3. For the full **8-week view**, go straight to `/personalcalendar`. You can browse day by day and click through to any game's store page.
- **Mobile app:** Valve's announcement and docs only name the store front page and the dedicated page. Neither mentions a mobile-app entry point, so we couldn't confirm one. The URL should still open in a phone browser.
- **Settings:** Nothing in Valve's posts says you need to turn anything on. It's no longer a Labs opt-in.

**What it shows**
- Recently released and upcoming games picked for you, with the 8-week window moving forward as time passes ([Valve](https://store.steampowered.com/news/posts/4149575031735702629)).
- [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2296237/steam-rolls-out-personal-calendar-feature-that-constantly-updates-recommended-games/) reports DLC and 1.0 filters. We couldn't verify those in Valve's text.

**How it's personalized**
- **Playtime:** It looks at the games you play the most. A few minutes in a new game barely moves it.
- **Similar players:** It finds players with similar playtime (Valve's docs also mention achievements) and shows what *they* wishlist and play ([docs](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/marketing/visibility/personalcalendar)).
- **Your own wishlist and follows:** Valve doesn't describe either as a direct input. The ingamenews line about "your wishlist" is a loose paraphrase. The wishlists that count are similar players' wishlists.
- Retrained **daily**, though day-to-day changes are small.
- **No paid placement and no hand curation.** It's fully algorithmic, per Valve.

**How it started**
- It launched as a **Steam Labs experiment in October 2025** and graduated to a full store feature on **Oct 23, 2026** after 11 months of feedback ([Valve](https://store.steampowered.com/news/posts/4149575031735702629); [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/games/1017994/steams-personal-calendar-feature-is-exiting-beta)).

**About the source:** The [ingamenews](https://ingamenews.com/gaming-news-updates/) item is a two-sentence wire blurb. It doesn't say where to find the feature, and it doesn't link Valve.

**What it means for devs (analysis)**
- **Eligibility:** You need a visible Coming Soon page with a specific release date. Valve advises setting it at least 60 days out for the dedicated page and at least 3 weeks out for the front page ([docs](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/marketing/visibility/personalcalendar)).
- **Indies:** There's no wishlist threshold, and picks are per player rather than by raw popularity. That gives niche games a real shot with the right audience. More wishlists still help.
- **Dates:** A delay of more than 24 hours inside the last two weeks before launch drops your game off the calendar until release. Lock your date before you get that close.
- **Mobile devs:** This is a Steam (PC) store surface. It only matters if you ship a Steam build, like PC ports of mobile games.

items.headline_md: Factorio 2.1 is out as the game's final major content update
items.summary_md: It adds mixed rocket cargo, better space logistics and native ARM64 Linux support.

sections.title: Video Game Emulation
sections.body_md: **Wii U lifter watch:** still no public repo for the r/decomps Wii U-to-x86 lifter. **PS5 / Switch 2:** no new breakthroughs found today. Reddit couldn't be read from my computer this morning.

items.headline_md: Update: LAS Recomp (Link's Awakening, Switch-to-PC) shipped Beta 5 Hotfix 2 last night
items.summary_md: It fixes black screens on older Intel graphics, a Mali crash, vanishing randomizer underwater items and a crash with accented names. The README now lists minimum specs. Still beta, not yet the stable build you're waiting for.

items.headline_md: Crackdown Recomp 1.0 (Xbox 360 to PC) is out with multithreaded rendering that roughly doubles frame rates
items.summary_md: It also supports up to 4K internal resolution and wide aspect ratios.

items.headline_md: Project Midas brings GoldenEye 007 to PC and Linux from the N64 decomp
items.summary_md: It adds widescreen, mouse look and modern controllers, needs your own dump, and already has a 1.0.1 patch.

items.headline_md: Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix (XBLA) got its first playable PC static recomp
FFTARecomp 3.0 (Final Fantasy Tactics Advance) adds a native Android build
items.summary_md: The PC install shrank from about 800 MB to about 11 MB.

items.headline_md: MediEvil II and Jersey Devil (PS1) got alpha native PC recomps built with psxrecomp
items.summary_md: Both are early alphas.

items.headline_md: Update: Clayface is heading for a $24–25M #1 opening from 3,458 theaters
items.summary_md: Friday was $10.4M including $3.5M in previews, with an A- CinemaScore, 76% critics and 93% audience on RT, against a reported $40M budget.

items.headline_md: You Can See Everything (A24) rose 22–28% in its second weekend to $19–20M
items.summary_md: Its total is about $44.6–45.6M.

items.headline_md: Wildwood opened to about $11M, and Wicker to $5.5–6M
items.summary_md: Both are new this weekend.

items.headline_md: Street Fighter fell 74% to $8.15M, for a $46.4M total
items.summary_md: That's about 25% behind Mortal Kombat 2 at the same point.
